questions.question: Describe how to draw a one-to-one pictograph of the fruit survey, apple 9, banana 7, orange 5, mango 8, grapes 3.
questions.expected_answer: Draw one same-size picture for each learner in neat rows: 9 apples, 7 bananas, 5 oranges, 8 mangoes and 3 bunches of grapes. Label each row, add a title such as Favourite fruit of Grade 4B, and draw a key showing that one picture stands for one learner.

questions.question: Explain the rules for the scale on a bar graph.
questions.expected_answer: The scale goes up the vertical axis, starts at 0, and goes up in equal steps, such as 1s, 2s or 5s. The steps are chosen so that the biggest number fits on the page.

questions.question: The reading groups read 18, 24, 12, 20 and 16 books. Choose a graph and a scale and explain your choice.
questions.expected_answer: A bar graph, because drawing 24 pictures would take too long. A scale counting in 2s from 0 to 26 fits the biggest number, 24, and every bar ends on a mark because all the numbers are even.
